question.text: In exchange-traded IROs, what happens when an option expires out-of-the-money?

answer.text: The option expires worthless and the buyer loses the premium paid
The buyer receives a partial refund of the premium
The option is automatically rolled over to the next expiry
The exchange pays the buyer a minimum settlement amount

explanation.text: The Logic: When an option expires OTM, it has zero intrinsic value and expires worthless. The buyer's loss is the entire premium paid, and the seller keeps the premium. The Trap: There is no partial refund, automatic rollover, or minimum settlement. The premium is fully at risk for the buyer. Cross-Exam Context: OTM expiry outcomes are tested in all NISM derivative modules -- the concept is universal.
